Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  soft labour / data-heavy week
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB on hold / easing optionality
🇨🇳 China  Bearish  less stimulus / weak credit
🇦🇺 Australia  Bearish  hiking bias / softer spending
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  MPC pause / March decision
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Rotation out of US tech, into the real economy
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
$NVDA  the payee of $650 billion in capex  ↑
$STLA  EV reset without a dividend floor  ↓
Gold / GLD  "retail calls it a bubble"
body: Monday, February 09 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The US enters a data-heavy week with a split picture: consumer sentiment rose to a six-month high in early February Reuters [Feb 06], while the Fed's Daly said the job market feels ‘precarious’ and is eyeing rate cuts Reuters [Feb 06]. The delayed January payrolls report lands on Feb. 11 Bloomberg.com [Feb 04], followed by inflation and retail sales data Investopedia [Feb 08]. We stay Mixed: households feel better than the hiring data suggest, and the payrolls print decides which side wins.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.50% and the 10Y at 4.22%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 72 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y rose 1 bp and the 10Y 3 bps, so the spread widened just 2 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and the 20-observation move is little changed; over five observations the 10Y fell 4 bps and the 2Y 2 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06). The 3M bill at 3.68% sits above the 2Y, so the market still prices cuts ahead (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06).

New / Most Important: Friday's rebound was broad: the Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time as Nvidia soared and traders refocused on AI spending Reuters [Feb 06]. The S&P 500 rose 1.97% to 6,932.30 and the Russell 2000 3.6%, while the VIX fell 1.4 points to 20.37 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Over five sessions the S&P 500 was still down 0.1% and the Nasdaq 100 1.87%, so the week ended as a rotation into cyclicals and small caps rather than a return to tech leadership (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Playbook ✓: Keep the cyclical and small-cap tilt that Friday confirmed, funded from long-duration software. Into the Feb. 11 payrolls Bloomberg.com [Feb 04], hold 2s10s steepeners: a weak print validates Daly's cut talk and pulls the 2Y below its 20-observation-ago 3.49%, while a strong print would push the front end up and is the trigger to take profits (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06). Hedge with S&P 500 put spreads while the VIX holds above 20.

Macro Stance: ECB policymakers are fretting over the risk of too-low inflation Reuters [Feb 06], which turns the next move from a hold into a possible cut. Low inflation and a central bank with an easing bias are a supportive mix for European equities: Bullish.

Activity & Inflation: With policymakers worried about undershooting inflation Reuters [Feb 06], a softer euro is welcome: EUR/USD closed at 1.1778, down 1.57% over five sessions, easing the currency drag on exporters (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). GBP/USD fell 2.07% over five sessions to 1.3521, which helps UK exporters in the FTSE 100 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

New / Most Important: Europe's STOXX 600 rebounded in broad-based gains on Friday while the Stellantis plunge dragged auto stocks Reuters [Feb 06]. Europe and Asia led global equity fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure Reuters [Feb 06], and the STOXX 600 closed at 617.12, up 0.89% on the day and 1.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Playbook ✓: Overweight European banks, industrials and the UK large-cap index; underweight autos until the EV write-down cycle is digested. A weaker euro after the ECB's dovish tilt helps exporters, so add DAX exposure — still down 2.14% over 20 sessions — on any confirmation of the orders rebound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Change the call if fund inflows reverse back toward US tech.

Macro Stance: Beijing has signalled a trimmed GDP growth target that requires less stimulus Bloomberg.com [Feb 05], and nothing over the weekend changed that. Factory surveys are mixed while credit and property stay weak, so the domestic cycle depends on policy that is being deliberately rationed. We stay Bearish on the domestic economy and on Hong Kong-listed platforms.

PMIs & Activity: The latest prints are January's: the official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30], while the private gauge showed factory activity growing at the fastest pace since October CNBC [Feb 01]. The gap between surveys says exporters are fine and smaller domestic firms are not; a February official PMI back above 50 would be the first sign of broader recovery.

Credit Impulse: New bank loans in 2025 were the lowest in seven years Reuters [Jan 15], and the January figure is still pending. A Reuters poll expects January bank lending to rise on predictable monetary policy Reuters [Feb 08], but January is seasonally the strongest month for loans, so a rise alone proves little. The test is household borrowing: without it, any January jump is front-loaded corporate and government credit.

Property: There is no fresh property print in the feed beyond January's ‘bleak start’, when sales declines accelerated South China Morning Post [Feb 02]. Shanghai is buying small older flats to revive its ailing housing market South China Morning Post [Feb 03], which supports one city but does not fix developer funding. What would confirm a bottom: tier-one sales stabilising after the Lunar New Year holiday.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing tightened its crypto crackdown, barring unapproved issuance of yuan-linked stablecoins abroad Bloomberg.com [Feb 06], a sign that capital-account control outranks financial innovation. On minerals, Washington defended its new alliance and rejected claims it targets China South China Morning Post [Feb 06], while rare-earth prices hit record highs amid China's export curbs against Japan Nikkei Asia [Feb 07] — Beijing is using its supply lever selectively.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng fell 1.21% to 26,559.95 and is down 3.02% over five sessions, and the Shanghai Composite closed at 4,065.58, down 1.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). In New York, ASHR rose 1.45% to 33.68 and KWEB 2.82% to 34.31, but KWEB is still down 4.48% over 20 sessions; USD/CNY held at 6.9378, a 0.65% yuan gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Friday's New York bounce in Chinese ADRs did not carry into Hong Kong, which still trades on the domestic demand story.

New / Most Important: China's central bank bought gold for a 15th consecutive month Reuters [Feb 06], extending a reserve diversification that supports gold on dips. Combined with the stablecoin ban, the message is a steady push for currency control and reserve independence rather than demand stimulus. For investors, that favours a firm yuan and gold over Chinese consumption equities.

Playbook ✓: Stay underweight KWEB and Hong Kong platforms until the January credit data are clear; a January loan print with a strong household component is the trigger to cover. Prefer long-CNY and gold over Chinese equity beta, and avoid developers. ⚠ Divergence: the private PMI at its fastest pace since October CNBC [Feb 01] says activity is firmer than our weak-demand call implies.

Macro Stance: Prime Minister Takaichi's party won a supermajority in Japan's lower house AP News [Feb 08], a mandate that removes coalition constraints on her spending agenda. Bloomberg reads the win as priming Japanese stocks for gains while damping the yen and bonds Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]. A strong government with a reflation agenda is Bullish for domestic equities, though households are lagging: real wages fell every month in 2025 Reuters [Feb 08].

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 156.784, up 2.36% over five sessions, and the Nikkei 225 at 54,253.68, up 0.81% on Friday and 6.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Japanese markets are set for a renewed ‘Takaichi trade’ Reuters [Feb 08], and Finance Minister Katayama is ready to talk with the market on Monday if needed Bloomberg.com [Feb 08] — a clear intervention warning around the yen.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities with a bias to banks, defence and capex names, and keep yen exposure hedged only partially because intervention risk caps USD/JPY. Fade any JGB selloff only after the government publishes spending numbers. Change the call if the yen weakens sharply despite official warnings, which would raise the odds of a disorderly bond move.

Macro Stance: Australian household spending fell in December after two strong months Reuters [Feb 08], while the RBA delivered its first rate rise in two years and left the door open for more AFR [Feb 03]. Governor Bullock has said government spending is putting pressure on inflation AFR [Feb 06], so the policy mix is a tighter central bank leaning against a loose budget. That is Bearish for consumer-facing equities.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD fell 1.12% to 0.6916 on Friday but is up 3.21% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 dropped 2.03% to 8,708.80, flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Higher mortgage rates and weaker December spending point to slower consumption in the first quarter, which caps upside for domestic earnings.

Playbook ✓: Underweight Australian discretionary retailers and REITs, prefer miners and banks. Hold AUD longs on dips toward its 20-session-ago 0.6701 while the RBA keeps a hiking bias (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Change the call if January spending data rebound, which would make further hikes likelier and favour banks over all else.

Monetary & Activity: The Monetary Policy Council's new projection sees inflation in line with the NBP target, with key decisions in March Business Insider Polska [Feb 06]. That leaves room for a cut once the council has its March data. A gradual easing path with inflation at target is a supportive mix for Polish financials, whose loan books benefit from lower rates.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5848 and EUR/PLN at 4.2216, the latter up 0.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). EPOL rose 1.47% to 37.92 and is up 5.86% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20TR ETF closed at 67.46, up 3.59% over 20 sessions; Pekao is up 9.25% and PKO BP 6.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Parkiet notes the WIG20 is dominated by the financial sector Parkiet [Feb 06], which explains its resilience in the tech rout.

Companies: Orlen will reduce asset values by €592 million TVP World [Feb 07], yet the stock rose 3.5% on Friday and is up 15.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Poland wants to take over a large bank in Ukraine Money.pl [Feb 06], a strategic move for state-linked lenders. KGHM is still down 6.35% over five sessions and Allegro 10.64% over 20 sessions, the laggards of the large caps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Security & New Development: Poland awarded the Kongsberg-PGZ consortium a $1.65 billion counter-drone system contract The Defense Post [Feb 02], adding to a defence build-out that supports domestic industry. The security premium is not weighing on the currency: EUR/PLN has barely moved over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Polish banks (Pekao, PKO BP) through EPOL or the WIG20TR ETF into the March decision; a gradual cut supports loan volumes more than it hurts margins. Avoid KGHM and Allegro until their 20-session trends turn. Change the call if the złoty weakens sharply on global risk-off. ⚠ Divergence: Orlen's €592 million write-down TVP World [Feb 07] coexists with a 15.13% 20-session rally in the stock, a sign that index buyers are ignoring company-level damage (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Narrative: The software rout paused: XLK rose 4.06% on Friday but is still down 2.16% over 20 sessions, and MSFT is down 16.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Strategists now say the selloff ‘probably seems overdone’ Yahoo Finance [Feb 08], but AI-disruption risk to seat-based software has not been disproved.

Reported: Thomson Reuters delivered solid results and guidance that were not enough to quell AI disruption fears Morningstar [Feb 06]. The pattern holds: in-line or better numbers do not lift software names while the terminal-value debate is open.

EPS Upside Watch: Hardware with pricing power: AAPL is up 7.37% over 20 sessions, and ORCL bounced 4.65% on Friday after a brutal run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Upside revisions are likelier for hardware and infrastructure vendors than for application software.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bounce came without a software-specific catalyst, and a rally that rests on positioning rather than news is fragile. Treat Friday as a short-covering rally, not a regime change: wait for a software print that rallies on in-line guidance before adding.

Narrative: Communication services is split between capex-heavy platforms and AI-assisted ad winners: XLC is down 1.46% over 20 sessions, GOOGL fell 2.53% on Friday and META is down 7.68% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Investors are pricing the cost of AI build-outs before the revenue.

Reported: Roblox jumped 16% after its earnings report Barron's [Feb 06], the clearest case of the market paying for user and bookings growth. DIS rose 3.55% on Friday but is down 4.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

EPS Upside Watch: Engagement-driven platforms with low capex needs have the best revision setup, because they monetise AI tools without building data centres. NFLX, down 9.2% over 20 sessions, prices a lot of competitive damage already (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The market is now punishing the AI builders inside the sector and rewarding the AI users: Roblox jumped after its report while GOOGL lost 4.48% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Pair long asset-light platforms against capex-heavy megacaps until capex guidance stops rising.

Narrative: Financials split in two: banks rallied with the cyclicals — JPM rose 3.95% and GS 4.31% on Friday — while private credit worries resurfaced in the $3 trillion market as AI pressures software firms CNBC [Feb 08]. XLF is still down 2.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Reported: Carlyle allayed software fears as private-equity deals boosted profit Reuters [Feb 06], and SocGen unveiled a €1.5 billion buyback after a profit beat Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. Alternative managers that can show deal flow are being separated from pure lenders to software.

EPS Upside Watch: Deposit-rich US banks: BAC is up 6.26% over five sessions, and a 72 bps 10Y−2Y spread supports net interest income (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06). European banks returning capital have the strongest revision momentum.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Private credit stocks keep falling as the software wipeout spreads Bloomberg.com [Feb 06], even as banks rally — the risk has moved off bank balance sheets and into the private funds. Own banks, avoid listed private-credit vehicles until loan marks are published.

Narrative: Energy keeps leading: XLE rose 1.99% on Friday and 14.39% over 20 sessions, with XOM up 21.27%, while Brent closed at 68.05, up 9.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Hedge funds hiked bullish oil bets to a 10-month high on Iran risks Bloomberg.com [Feb 06].

Reported: Shell posted its weakest quarterly profit in nearly five years but kept buybacks steady CNBC [Feb 05], and CVX is up 13.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The market is paying for capital return rather than earnings growth in this group.

EPS Upside Watch: Iran remains the swing factor: Tehran called the Oman talks a ‘good start’ that will continue Reuters [Feb 07], so the premium is not about to collapse, nor is it escalating. Producers with low breakevens benefit most from a range-bound but elevated crude price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Saudi Arabia cut its flagship oil price to Asia for a fourth straight month WSJ [Feb 06] — the physical market is softer than the futures positioning suggests. With hedge-fund longs at a 10-month high, a diplomatic surprise would hit crowded positioning; keep integrateds, trim high-beta E&Ps.

Narrative: Industrials led the rally: CAT rose 7.06% on Friday and 19.42% over 20 sessions, GE 4.78% on the day, and XLI is up 8.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The Dow's first close above 50,000 Reuters [Feb 06] is an industrial and cyclical milestone more than a tech one.

Reported: There was no major new industrial print in the latest sessions, so price action did the talking: Boeing rose 2.57% on Friday and is up 6.88% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The market keeps paying for order books tied to power and aviation.

EPS Upside Watch: Power equipment and aerospace suppliers have the clearest backlog visibility, with Big Tech capex near record levels supporting electrical demand. CAT's 20-session move shows how quickly the market prices that visibility.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Defence is the exception: investors in defence stocks are wary as Trump places new limits on CEO pay and dividends Reuters [Feb 06]. Favour commercial aerospace and power equipment over US defence primes until the payout rules are clear.

Narrative: Discretionary is the laggard of the rotation: XLY is down 4.01% over 20 sessions, and AMZN fell 5.55% on Friday and 14.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The index heavyweights now trade on capex and margins, not on the consumer.

Reported: Amazon shares slid as its $200 billion outlay fanned fears over AI returns Reuters [Feb 06]. TSLA rose 3.5% on Friday but is still down 5.67% over 20 sessions, so the sector's two heavyweights are both capex stories (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

EPS Upside Watch: Improving consumer sentiment helps upper-income retailers and home improvement: HD is up 7.12% over 20 sessions and NKE rose 1.95% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The upside is in idiosyncratic turnarounds, not the index heavyweights.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Better sentiment has not lifted the sector because its largest name is now a capex story, not a consumer one. Underweight XLY versus equal-weight discretionary until Amazon's capex guide stops rising.

Narrative: Staples are massively outperforming the market Yahoo Finance [Feb 08]: XLP is up 12.11% over 20 sessions, WMT 16.02% and COST 9.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The bid is a rotation into real-economy cash flows as investors cut exposure to AI spenders.

Reported: WMT rose 3.34% on Friday and 10.11% over five sessions, and COST closed above 1,000 at 1,001.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Scale retailers with e-commerce and membership income are being treated as both defensive and growth.

EPS Upside Watch: Big-box grocers remain the likeliest beats; branded packaged food with weaker pricing power is not. Coca-Cola's report is on the week's calendar Investopedia [Feb 08], a test of whether pricing power survives the volume push.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are now a momentum trade, which changes their risk: a strong payrolls report that lifts cyclicals and yields would hit the group's stretched multiples first. Keep the overweight in retailers, take profits in branded staples.

Narrative: Health care is stabilising but policy-capped: XLV rose 1.85% on Friday and is down 0.26% over 20 sessions, while UNH is still down 20.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The White House unveiled TrumpRx, a discounted-drugs website Reuters [Feb 06].

Reported: Bristol Myers forecast an upbeat 2026 and expects an Eliquis price cut to pay off Reuters [Feb 06] — a template for accepting lower prices in exchange for volume. LLY rose 3.66% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

EPS Upside Watch: Companies that trade price for volume under the new pricing regime, as Bristol Myers is doing, have the clearest path to beating lowered estimates. Distributors also benefit from volume growth without price exposure.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The WSJ argues the weight-loss price wars are breaking Big Pharma's business model WSJ [Feb 07]. If that is right, the GLP-1 trade shifts from pricing power to volume share — prefer the volume leader and avoid challengers that need premium pricing.

Narrative: Materials have rejoined the rotation: XLB is up 8.44% over 20 sessions, gold closed at 4,979.80, up 4.95% over five sessions, and copper at 5.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). China's central bank bought gold for a 15th consecutive month Reuters [Feb 06], a steady official bid under the price.

Reported: The failed Rio Tinto-Glencore talks show big copper deals are hard to do WSJ [Feb 06], which keeps scarce copper assets valued on their own cash flows. FCX is up 11.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners after the shakeout: NEM rose 6.26% on Friday and is up 7.89% over 20 sessions, and higher realised prices feed straight into earnings (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Copper producers benefit from data-centre and grid demand meeting constrained supply.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver has not recovered with gold: SI=F is down 1.99% over five sessions while gold is up (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The speculative leg of the metals trade broke; the official-sector leg did not — own gold and copper, not silver.

Narrative: REITs are participating modestly: XLRE rose 1.84% on Friday and is up 3.83% over 20 sessions, with the 10Y at 4.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06). Rates are not the driver; the rotation out of tech is.
Reported: The White House is considering an antitrust probe into homebuilders Reuters [Feb 06], a new policy risk for housing-linked equities.
EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and industrial landlords remain the cleanest growth, as Big Tech's capex wave needs space and power. Residential REITs benefit if the homebuilder probe slows new supply.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A probe aimed at builders could help landlords: less aggressive new supply supports rents. Prefer apartment and single-family rental REITs over homebuilders until the scope of the probe is known.

Narrative: Data centres dominate rising US power demand growth Axios [Feb 06], and utilities with regulated rate bases capture it. XLU is up 3.24% over 20 sessions and NEE 12.56%, while CEG bounced 5.81% on Friday but is down 18.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Reported: Xcel Energy is pursuing large-load tariffs in 4 states amid data-centre growth Utility Dive [Feb 06], a model that makes data-centre customers pay for the capacity they require. That protects households and the regulatory bargain.

EPS Upside Watch: Utilities that lock in large-load tariffs before building capacity have the best earnings visibility; Entergy's results on Feb. 12 Entergy [Feb 05] are the next read on data-centre load conversion.

⚡ Breaking Convention: New York Democrats propose a sweeping pause on data-centre construction Politico [Feb 06]. Affordability politics is spreading from bills into permits; favour regulated utilities in states with large-load tariffs over merchant generators.

Narrative: European autos took the week's biggest hit: STLA fell 23.69% on Friday and 34.12% over 20 sessions, and the STOXX Europe 600 autos ETF dropped 2.82% to 44.67, down 6.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Reported: Stellantis booked a €22 billion write-down on its EV reset and cancelled its dividend Automotive News [Feb 06], and its shares slumped over 20% after the $26.5 billion EV-related writedown Reuters [Feb 06]. The Stellantis-backed ACC then dropped plans for Italian and German gigafactories Reuters [Feb 07].

EPS Upside Watch: Little upside near term: write-downs reset book values but not demand. VOW3 is down 2.99% and BMW 3.89% over 20 sessions, holding up better than Stellantis but still falling (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The kitchen-sink reset could mark a capitulation low for Stellantis, but cancelled dividends remove the income buyers who usually step in. Stay underweight the sector; revisit only after a quarter of positive free cash flow.

Narrative: Big Tech is set to spend $650 billion this year as the AI race intensifies Bloomberg.com [Feb 06], and semis are the direct recipient. SOXX rose 5.34% on Friday and is up 9.05% over 20 sessions, with NVDA up 7.87% and TSM 5.48% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Reported: Tokyo Electron lifted its outlook in a sign of AI-spurred chip spending Bloomberg.com [Feb 06], confirming that the capex wave reaches equipment makers. ASML rose 4.66% on Friday and is up 18.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

EPS Upside Watch: Global chip sales are expected to hit $1 trillion this year, an industry group says Reuters [Feb 06]. Tight supply supports pricing across the chain: MU is up 20.69% and INTC 23.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia shares rose 8% as Jensen Huang said the $660 billion capex buildout is sustainable CNBC [Feb 06] — the market is now paying for the spending that it punishes in the spenders. That asymmetry favours owning suppliers (NVDA, TSM, memory, equipment) over the hyperscalers.

Rewarded: Roblox jumped 16% after its report Barron's [Feb 06], Tokyo Electron lifted its outlook on AI chip spending Bloomberg.com [Feb 06], Carlyle allayed software fears with stronger deal profits Reuters [Feb 06], and SocGen paired a beat with a €1.5 billion buyback Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. The common thread is visible cash: bookings, orders or capital return.

Punished: Amazon slid as its $200 billion outlay fanned fears over AI returns Reuters [Feb 06], Stellantis slumped over 20% on its EV writedown Reuters [Feb 06], and Thomson Reuters' solid guidance was not enough to quell AI disruption fears Morningstar [Feb 06]. MSFT, down 16.1% over 20 sessions, shows the same discount on AI spend without visible payback (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Pattern: Barron's sums up the season: tech had an awful earnings season, and other stocks are saving the day Barron's [Feb 06]. The market pays the receivers of AI capex and punishes the payers, and it pays old-economy companies for buybacks and order books.

Attention into EPS: The week's calendar brings Cisco, Coca-Cola, McDonald's and Ford Investopedia [Feb 08], and Entergy reports on Feb. 12 Entergy [Feb 05]. Cisco tests whether networking captures AI capex like chips do; Ford tests how deep the EV write-down cycle runs after Stellantis.

Playbook: Buy post-earnings strength in capex receivers and companies with buybacks; fade capex step-ups by the spenders unless revenue accelerates in the same quarter. The trigger to change the pattern is a hyperscaler that rallies on higher capex because its cloud revenue growth accelerates.

Attention Gap: While attention sits on US tech, the FT lays out three ways European banks are finding their mojo Financial Times [Feb 08], and SocGen just unveiled a €1.5 billion buyback after a profit beat Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. Europe also leads global equity fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure Reuters [Feb 06].

Exposure & Risk: Instruments: European bank ETFs or single names such as SocGen and BNP Paribas, and the Euro Stoxx 50 at 5,998.40, up 1.23% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Risk: an ECB cut on too-low inflation would compress margins, so prefer banks with fee income and large buybacks.

Attention Gap: Rare-earth prices hit record highs amid China's export curbs against Japan Nikkei Asia [Feb 07], while Washington is building a minerals alliance it says does not target China South China Morning Post [Feb 06]. The metals volatility of the past fortnight pulled attention to gold and silver and away from this supply squeeze.

Exposure & Risk: Instruments: rare-earth miners outside China and copper producers such as FCX at 60.67, up 11.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Risk: Chinese curbs can be lifted as quickly as they are imposed, and small-cap miners are illiquid; size positions accordingly.

Market Context: Bitcoin closed at 70,264.73 at the prior completed daily close, up 1.42% on the day but down 7.1% over five sessions and 24.08% over 20; Ether closed at 2,088.76, down 34.45% over 20 sessions, and Solana at 87.04, down 34.72% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-08). Friday's equity proxies bounced hard: IBIT rose 9.92%, COIN 13% and MSTR 26.11% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin rebounded above $70,000 after nearly breaking below $60,000 a day earlier CNBC [Feb 06], and BlackRock's ETF IBIT hit a $10 billion volume record, hinting at capitulation CoinDesk [Feb 06]. Strategy's CEO said Bitcoin would need to plunge to $8,000 before balance-sheet issues arise The Block [Feb 06], easing forced-seller fears. China barred unapproved issuance of yuan-linked stablecoins abroad Bloomberg.com [Feb 06].

Playbook: Record volume into a V-shaped reversal is a classic capitulation signature, so a starter position in IBIT is reasonable with a stop below the recent low. Prefer spot ETFs over treasury-company equities, which remain levered to sentiment. Add only if Bitcoin holds above its five-session-ago level; a break back below the capitulation low would reopen the downside.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 97.63, down 1.31% over 20 sessions, while TLT ended at 87.54 and IEF at 96.07, nearly unchanged on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The 10Y−2Y spread of 72 bps was little changed over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06), so the bond market is waiting for the payrolls and inflation prints rather than trading the equity rebound.

Credit Check: HYG rose 0.35% to 80.81 and LQD closed at 110.56, up 0.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Public credit is calm, but private credit worries have resurfaced as AI pressures software borrowers CNBC [Feb 08] — the stress is in the private market, not in index spreads.

Portfolio Implication: Europe and Asia are leading global equity fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure Reuters [Feb 06]. Stay overweight ex-US equities, cyclicals and real assets; keep IG over HY and avoid listed private-credit vehicles. Reassess if the payrolls print is strong enough to pull flows back into US growth.

What Is Priced: The delayed January jobs report arrives on Feb. 11 Bloomberg.com [Feb 04], with inflation and retail sales data following Investopedia [Feb 08]. Daly's ‘precarious’ labour market comment and a 2Y at 3.50%, below the 3M bill at 3.68%, show cuts are partly priced (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-06).

Conditional Expression: A weak payrolls print plus soft inflation would validate cuts: own 2Y Treasuries, small caps (Russell 2000 at 2,670.34) and homebuilder-sensitive names, and sell the dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). A strong print with sticky inflation would push the front end up and hit staples and utilities that have run on defensive flows; then rotate into banks and energy.

Risk: Two delayed releases in one week concentrate event risk, and a shutdown-distorted print could be revised heavily. Keep position sizes moderate into the data and use options for directional bets.

What Is Priced: With a supermajority secured, Japanese markets are set for a renewed ‘Takaichi trade’ Reuters [Feb 08] — Bloomberg expects gains for stocks and pressure on the yen and bonds Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]. The Nikkei 225 is already up 6.14% over 20 sessions and USD/JPY sits at 156.784 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06).

Conditional Expression: If the spending plan is modest and funded, own Japanese equities and banks and fade yen weakness near official warning levels. If it is larger than expected, JGB yields rise and the yen weakens until intervention — then hold equities but hedge with yen calls and underweight life insurers.

Risk: Finance Minister Katayama is ready to talk with the market if needed Bloomberg.com [Feb 08]; verbal intervention can reverse the yen leg of the trade in hours. Avoid leveraged short-yen positions.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia rose 8% on Friday as Jensen Huang said the $660 billion capex buildout is sustainable CNBC [Feb 06], after Big Tech's spending plans reached about $650 billion for the year Bloomberg.com [Feb 06]. Thesis: the market punishes the spenders but pays the suppliers, and Nvidia is the largest supplier.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 185.41, up 7.87% on Friday and 0.2% over 20 sessions, just above its 20-session-ago 185.04 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Risk: if a hyperscaler trims capex, suppliers would fall faster than spenders; a close back below the 20-session-ago level would signal the rebound has failed.

Catalyst & Thesis: Stellantis booked a €22 billion write-down on its EV reset and cancelled its dividend Automotive News [Feb 06], and the battery venture it backs dropped plans for two gigafactories Reuters [Feb 07]. Thesis: without a dividend, income investors exit, and the reset does not restore demand or pricing.

Price Hurdle & Risk: STLA closed at 7.28, down 23.69% on Friday and 34.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Risk: a kitchen-sink charge can mark a low and short interest can squeeze; cover on a close back above the pre-announcement level.

Catalyst & Thesis: Entergy reports full-year 2025 results on Feb. 12 Entergy [Feb 05]. With data centres dominating rising US power demand growth Axios [Feb 06] and Xcel pushing large-load tariffs Utility Dive [Feb 06], the thesis is that regulated utilities convert data-centre demand into rate-base growth with protected returns.

Price Hurdle & Risk: ETR is not on our market card, so we give no price level; the sector reference is XLU at 43.35, up 3.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Risk: political pushback such as the New York construction-pause proposal Politico [Feb 06] could spread to Entergy's states.

Observed Attention: Hong Kong retail investors snapped up bitcoin amid the crypto crash South China Morning Post [Feb 06], and IBIT's record $10 billion volume day CoinDesk [Feb 06] shows how much money moved through the ETF in both directions.

Motivation & Bias: Buy-the-dip conditioning and anchoring to prior highs: a 24.08% 20-session drop in Bitcoin looks like a discount to holders who remember higher prices (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-08). The bias ignores that leverage, not value, drove the fall.

Instrument & Risk: IBIT closed at 39.68, up 9.92% on Friday but down 22.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). Use staged entries and a hard stop; volatility at these levels can erase a week's gain in a session.

Observed Attention: A survey finds 55% of individual investors see a bubble in gold CNBC [Feb 06], even as the metal rebounded. Retail attention has shifted from buying the dip to questioning the rally.
Motivation & Bias: Recency bias after the crash makes investors wary, while official buyers keep accumulating. That mismatch tends to favour patient holders over short-term traders.

Instrument & Risk: GLD closed at 455.46, up 3.07% on Friday and 10.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The risk is another margin-driven shakeout; hold physical-backed ETFs rather than leveraged products.

Observed Attention: MSTR rose 26.11% on Friday yet is still down 9.87% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06), and the CEO's claim that Bitcoin would need to plunge to $8,000 before balance-sheet issues arise The Block [Feb 06] gave dip-buyers a floor to anchor on.
Motivation & Bias: Retail treats MSTR as a leveraged Bitcoin call and buys it hardest after sharp drops — a lottery-ticket preference for convexity.

Instrument & Risk: MSTR closed at 134.93, still down 19.19% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-06). The stock amplifies Bitcoin both ways; size positions as if they were twice as volatile as IBIT.

Observed Attention: Business Insider reports that ‘Big Short’ investor Michael Burry's pick for the next Warren Buffett is GameStop's Ryan Cohen Business Insider [Feb 07], reviving attention on the original meme stock.
Motivation & Bias: Authority bias: a famous contrarian's endorsement gives retail permission to buy, regardless of operating results.
Instrument & Risk: GME is not on our market card, so no price level. Meme rallies driven by endorsements fade quickly; use defined-risk options or stay out.
